Subject: Mutual action blueprint + launch pack: staged switchover & evaluation regimen

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the productive close call today. Per our conversation I’m attaching an initial mutual action blueprint (MAP) and an evaluation regimen doc so we have a single source for sequencing the work after signature. Key asks in this draft:

- Confirm preferred canary window (we proposed two 72-hour windows, see tab 'Canary Options' in MAP-launch-pack-v1.xlsx).
- Pick training cohorts (ProdReadiness vs. AdminOps) and preferred week for train-the-trainer.
- Any migration blackout constraints for your platform team (database schema freeze / backups).

High-level proposed cadence:
1) Week 0: Contract executed & kickoff; access provisioning; SSO & KMS handoff.
2) Week 1–2: Canary cohort A (10% traffic), monitoring + evaluation tests from eval-regimen-v1.md.
3) Week 3: Training cohort 1 (trainers + QA).
4) Week 4–5: Incremental migration; full ramp if KPIs meet SLOs.

We left the go-live date as TBD in the MAP until you confirm the migration blackout and the training slot. If helpful, we can split the canary into three short windows instead of a continuous 72-hour run — note trade-offs in the Comments column.

Attachments: MAP-launch-pack-v1.xlsx (with timeline tabs), eval-regimen-v1.md (test matrix + pass/fail criteria). I’ve also linked a Jira ticket to track technical tasks: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/ONB-312

Next steps: if you can review and reply with the two preferred canary windows and trainer names by Friday (6/20), we’ll lock the kickoff agenda and schedule the technical runbook session.

Thanks —

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0142

Ben —

Appreciate you sending this over so quickly. I reviewed the MAP and eval regimen with our platform lead and the following items to flag: 

- Migration blackout: we have a weekly deploy freeze every Tuesday 02:00–06:00 UTC; we cannot run schema changes during that window.
- Canary windows: prefer shorter, discrete windows to limit blast radius. Can you propose two 24-hour windows (non-consecutive) in the week of July 7–13?
- Training: target week of July 14 for trainer sessions; our lead trainer is Darren Liu (darren.liu@orchardone.com).

We’ve attached a draft SOW for initial review (SOW-draft.pdf). A couple of commercial asks from procurement: we will need a 60-day retention option for audit logs, and a short note on encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.

I’ll loop in our security contact if you need a deeper dive on the KMS/HSM question.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Integrations
OrchardOne

Subject: Re: Mutual action blueprint + launch pack: staged switchover & evaluation regimen

Thanks Elaine — very helpful constraints. Quick notes and a revised option inline.

- On canary windows: we can run two separate 24-hour windows during July 7–13. Proposed slots (PDT): July 8 00:00–24:00 and July 11 00:00–24:00. Each slot will be configured as a traffic-slice (10% then 25% peak) with rollback hooks and automatic fallback to the previous model if error rate > 1% for more than 10 minutes.

- On migration freeze: we will avoid schema-affecting tasks during your Tuesday 02:00–06:00 UTC freeze. All DB migrations will be scheduled outside that window and validated in a parallel dry-run environment.

- On training: July 14 works. We'll run two 90-minute trainer sessions (11:00–12:30 PDT / 15:00–16:30 PDT) and provide a recording + quick reference guide. Please confirm Darren as trainer lead so we can add him to the trainer prep call on July 9.

- On retention & encryption: Ben, can you add a short blurb (1–2 paragraphs) to the MAP describing the 60-day optional retention and the CMK flow so Elaine can pass to procurement/security?

I’ve updated the 'Execution Options' tab in the MAP to reflect the July slots (see attached updated worksheet).

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com | +1 650-555-0210
